_note: ILLUSTRATIVE placeholder answers for the RC-1 Grid-to-Chip demo bid (OPP-0003), unit CLOUD (Flex cloud and rack-scale integration), P-49 part B: written for the PoC from the unit's point of view, not real unit positions. No certification, rating, figure or date in them is verified.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We will install and integrate the Owner-furnished equipment that falls in Lot 6 into our rack and system design, and treat it as part of the integrated system we test and hand over.
answers.conditions: The Owner's equipment list and delivery dates are confirmed during dialogue.
answers.next_steps: Ask for the Owner-furnished equipment list at the first dialogue session.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We will train the Owner's operations staff on the compute system, covering daily operation, monitoring, first-line repair and the management stack, as part of the Lot 6 price.
answers.next_steps: Agree the training plan and number of attendees with the Owner's team.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We will use the Owner's published PUE and energy price in our total cost of ownership figures for the compute system rather than our own assumptions.

Illustrative placeholder response: We offer the full compute system as integrated, liquid-cooled racks: control plane, GPU and CPU partitions, interconnect and multi-tier storage, with each GPU on its own high-speed network link, racks fed at 800 VDC and rack TDP stated per rack type. The hardware meets the memory, NVMe and network figures; the cloud-like service layer is not part of the Flex offer.
answers.reason: We integrate and support the hardware; the virtual machine, Kubernetes and Slurm service layer is not a Flex product and is not offered (capability gap REQ-0003-0109).
answers.conditions: The accelerator model is fixed at the technical decision point.
answers.next_steps: Confirm the accelerator platform before the final tender.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our design keeps each deployment unit below 20 MW under any workload, storage and network included, and we will state the maximum power in total and per partition.
answers.conditions: Final figures follow the configuration fixed at the technical decision point.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: The system provides power controls at system, rack, node and component level with stated reaction times, warns ahead of draw changes above 1 MW over 15 minutes, and supports a sequenced full-system power up and down with described timings. Board and sub-component control depends on what the chosen accelerator platform exposes.
answers.reason: Board and sub-component power controls are set by the accelerator and board vendors, so we can only commit to the controls their platform provides.
answers.next_steps: Confirm the board and sub-component controls with the accelerator vendor and state reaction times in the final tender.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: The system is designed with no single point of failure: it keeps running, at worst degraded, after the loss of any one field-replaceable unit, server or switch, and supports rolling upgrades with at least half in production. We will propose availability, mean time between interrupts and job mean time to interrupt, and show how we derived them.
answers.conditions: Reliability figures are derived from the final configuration and component failure data.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: The system's security design is compatible with ISO/IEC 27001, with strict tenant isolation including network traffic, and we will patch firmware, drivers and software throughout the maintenance period.
answers.reason: Fix times for high or critical vulnerabilities depend on when the component vendors release a fix, so we cannot commit to the Owner's policy deadlines unchanged.
answers.workaround: A joint patch policy: fixes applied within the Owner's deadlines once the vendor releases them, with agreed interim mitigations until then.
answers.next_steps: Review the Owner's vulnerability policy during dialogue.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Storage is offered in tiers: a POSIX parallel file system and capacity object storage, both expandable without interruption and accessed over POSIX, NFS and S3.
answers.conditions: File system software is from a storage partner, integrated and supported by us.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: The control-plane network is kept separate from the compute and storage network, tenants are securely partitioned, and our hall layout keeps links between halls within 500 m.
answers.conditions: Hall layout is confirmed in the network plan.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We will provide five years of maintenance and support from acceptance, 24 by 7, with a four-hour response, concurrent maintenance and six hours for cabinet-level concurrent repairs.
answers.reason: Two hours for every other repair is not realistic for every fault, for example where a part has to be swapped and re-tested.
answers.workaround: Two hours to restore service using the on-site spares, and a full repair within eight hours.
answers.next_steps: Agree the repair definitions during dialogue.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We will keep an on-site parts cache sized for two weeks of normal repairs, plus spare nodes of at least 1% of each node type, and refill it as parts are used.

Illustrative placeholder response: We will run MLPerf Storage, IOR, BigDataBench, Ray Train, Horovod, MLPerf Training and MLPerf Inference on the offered system, and will add benchmarks the Owner asks for.
answers.conditions: Benchmarks added later are scheduled and scoped with the Owner.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We will deliver in phases: control plane, storage and network with a minimal set of compute nodes first, and a test system with a minimal management stack as soon as possible after contract signing.
answers.next_steps: Include the phase plan in the project plan.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our racks and compute equipment are designed to tolerate any disturbance that is foreseeable within the Section 9 interface limits on the power, cooling and telemetry they receive.
answers.conditions: Applies to the Lot 6 side of each interface.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: As integrator we confirm the interface schedule between the lots offered: the 800 VDC input, busduct, row busway and interlocked whips (IF-03 to IF-05, distribution side), the 54 VDC in-rack bus from the 800 to 54 VDC shelf (IF-06), facility water up to 45 °C at the CDU with the stated secondary loop (IF-07), and telemetry and control from our equipment to Lot 6 (IF-09).
answers.reason: The sides that belong to scope not offered in this tender are not confirmed: the power-block output to Lot 3 (IF-03, power-block side), the power-block telemetry over Modbus TCP/IP (IF-09) and the chiller supply of IF-08.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We accept acceptance from factory tests through the 30-day availability test, and will time our deliverables against award and first delivery.

Illustrative placeholder response: We will agree the pre-delivery assembly, quality and factory test plan at least 30 days before the factory test, covering burn-in, benchmarks and fault injection such as pulled cables, powered-down subsystems and known bad parts.

Illustrative placeholder response: We plan for a 60-day acceptance period with a functionality demonstration, a system test with two cold boots, a resilience test with fault injection, five runs of each benchmark and a 30-day contiguous availability test.
Illustrative placeholder response: We accept no upgrades and no open critical bugs in the last seven days of the availability test.
answers.reason: Counting every repair that causes downtime as an outage would also count repairs on a single node that do not affect users, so we accept this only for repairs that take down a partition or the service.
answers.next_steps: Agree the outage definition in the acceptance test plan.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We accept liquidated damages for missed service levels, capped by the at-risk amounts described, and delay penalties that scale with the length of the delay and the seriousness of the breach, subject to an aggregate cap on liquidated damages and delay penalties together.
answers.reason: Liquidated damages and delay penalties have no overall limit as written, which leaves an open-ended risk on a phased multi-lot delivery.
answers.workaround: An aggregate cap on liquidated damages and delay penalties together, set as a percentage of each lot's price; the percentage is stated in the financial offer and listed in the commercial exceptions schedule (CT-08).

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our commercial exceptions are listed in the separate exceptions schedule and kept to a minimum: on liquidated damages, only the aggregate cap per lot asked for under CT-07; any indexed price is shown there only as an alternative to the firm price.

Illustrative placeholder response: Warranty is included in the five-year maintenance period, with component warranties running inside it, and we accept responsibility for failures caused by foreseeable disturbances within the Section 9 limits.

Illustrative placeholder response: We provide a supply-chain security and risk plan for the compute system, with last-time buys and alternative sources for sensitive components such as accelerators. Instead of a guarantee for each original component over the system's whole lifetime, we commit to the availability period stated as the proposed change.
answers.reason: No supplier can guarantee every original component for an open-ended system lifetime: electronic parts follow their makers' life cycles.
answers.workaround: Spare parts or compatible form-fit-function replacements available for at least 10 years from acceptance, with at least 12 months' notice of end of life and a last-time-buy offer before any component is discontinued.
